text.p: Engineering consultancy Heidemij said on Tuesday it is to change its name as part of a drive to increase internal corporate cohesion and raise its international profile.
"We are now in talks with consultants to seek a more appealing corporate name," Heidemij chairman Frans Luttmer told a results news conference.
He said the new name, yet to be decided and set to be unveiled some time in the autumn, would be used internationally but coupled in local markets to the group companies there.
Internally the firm was using the makeshift name "CEDIS".
As such the company would be known as CEDIS Geraghty in the U.S, for example, and CEDIS Heidemij in the Netherlands, Luttmer said.

He said the name change was expected to cost the company "a couple of million guilders" but added this extraordinary charge would be more than offset by book profits on the sale of environmental consultancy Fugro earlier this year.
Heidemij said in February the book profit from the sale would result in a net extraordinary gain of between 11 and 13 million guilders in 1997.
The name change was included in this figure, Luttmer said.
